SENIOR FINANCE EXECUTIVE, GRANTS

Job Purpose

The Senior Finance Executive, Grants is responsible for administering the organisation's grant portfolio by coordinating grant applications, monitoring grant utilisation, ensuring compliance with funding requirements, maintaining accurate grant records, and supporting grant reporting and audits. The role ensures grants are managed efficiently and in accordance with funding agency requirements and organisational policies.

Key Responsibilities

1. Grant Administration

  • Coordinate the administration of grants throughout the grant lifecycle, from award to closure.
  • Maintain accurate grant records and supporting documentation.
  • Monitor grant conditions and funding requirements to ensure compliance.
  • Liaise with internal stakeholders on grant administration matters.

2. Grant Tracking & Utilisation

  • Monitor grant utilisation against approved budgets and funding conditions.
  • Track grant balances, expenditure and utilisation to ensure timely use of funds.
  • Identify under-utilisation or overspending risks and escalate where appropriate.
  • Prepare regular grant utilisation reports for management.

3. Grant Financial Management

  • Prepare grant-related journals, reconciliations and supporting schedules.
  • Support grant income recognition and grant accrual accounting in accordance with accounting standards.
  • Coordinate grant claims, reimbursements and funding submissions where applicable.
  • Ensure grant transactions are accurately recorded within the ERP system.

4. Compliance, Audit & Reporting

  • Prepare grant reports required by funding agencies and management.
  • Ensure compliance with grant agreements, funding guidelines and regulatory requirements.
  • Coordinate grant audits and prepare supporting documentation for auditors.
  • Follow up and resolve audit observations and grant compliance issues.

5. Stakeholder Management

  • Work closely with programme owners, operational departments and finance teams to monitor grant performance.
  • Liaise with funding agencies on grant administration and reporting matters.
  • Provide guidance to departments on grant policies, utilisation and documentation requirements.

6. Process Improvement & Systems

  • Identify opportunities to improve grant management processes and strengthen controls.
  • Participate in ERP enhancements, finance transformation and grant system improvements.
  • Support the development of standard operating procedures and grant administration guidelines.
  • Promote best practices in grant governance and compliance.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's Degree in Accountancy, Finance, Business or equivalent.
  • Minimum 4–6 years of relevant experience in grant administration, finance or financial reporting.
  • Experience managing government or grant-funded programmes will be an advantage.
  • Good understanding of grant accounting, compliance and audit requirements.
  • Experience using ERP systems and Microsoft Excel.
  • Strong analytical, organisational and stakeholder management skills.

Competencies

  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Good financial analysis and reconciliation skills.
  • Excellent planning and organisational abilities.
  • Effective communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Problem-solving and analytical mindset.
  • Able to work independently and manage multiple deadlines.
  • Continuous improvement mindset with an interest in automation and process enhancement.

About St Lukes Eldercare

St Lukes ElderCare (SLEC) is a Christian healthcare provider dedicated to enriching the lives of seniors in Singapore, regardless of race, language and religion.

Guided by our GRACE philosophy of care, we are committed to providing compassionate and holistic care that fosters autonomy and choice. To empower elders of varying needs, from the fit to the frail, we offer a comprehensive suite of services islandwide. These include community based programmes that promote active ageing; centre-based offerings such as day care, rehabilitation and nursing; residential (nursing home) services for long-term care; and home based services covering medical, nursing and therapy needs.

Leveraging our legacy of over 25 years, we are on an unstoppable mission to transform care challenges of Singapore's ageing population. Through innovation, collaboration and education, we seek to elevate the community care sector, where elders thrive in their golden years and age with dignity, independence and joy.

Incorporated in 1999, SLEC is a registered charity and an Institution of a Public Character. Since our founding with four centres, we have grown to more than 30 centres and two nursing homes, impacting over 22,000 elders islandwide.

We are seeking a passionate and compassionate professional to join us. If you're ready to embrace a challenge that blends purpose with professional and personal growth, we invite you to join our Super Loving Extra Caring family to Serve, Love and Empower Communities together!

jobs.description:
Highlights:

Location: Cyprus

Language: Fluent in Russian and English (C1+)

About Fundraise Up

We’re Fundraise Up - a global fundraising platform built to make donating to nonprofits fast, seamless, and accessible to all. Every month, our technology powers tens of millions of dollars in donations across the globe. We focus on innovation that directly impacts results: faster load times, higher conversion rates, global payment support, and accessibility-first design.

Our platform is trusted by many of the world’s leading nonprofits, including UNICEF, the Alzheimer’s Association, and a wide range of global NGOs. With a 4.9/5 rating across top software review platforms, we’re recognized not just for our impact - but for the quality of the product we deliver.

A Truly Global Product

We operate in the enterprise segment, serving nonprofit organizations across North America, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Europe.

We’re building a large and complex product ecosystem that serves nonprofits, donors, and partners around the world. The platform includes a modern checkout experience and customizable widgets (each a standalone SPA), donor, organization, and partner portals, admin tools, and several internal apps.

The Team

We are a distributed team of 160+ product professionals. Our team members are mainly based across Spain, Poland, Portugal, Georgia, Armenia, Serbia, Turkey, and Cyprus.

Despite our scale, we operate like a focused team - where every task matters and every voice is heard. We value thoughtful collaboration, strong engineering practices, and a product mindset. You’ll be joining a team where quality, mentorship, and mutual respect come first.

About Peer-to-Peer at Fundraise Up

Peer-to-Peer turns supporters into fundraisers. Instead of only donating, a supporter creates a fundraising page, invites others to give, joins a team, or participates in an event on behalf of a nonprofit.

We are building Peer-to-Peer as a new product line. The product starts with two connected directions:

  • P2P DIY: self-serve fundraising for birthdays, memorials, personal challenges, and other supporter-led campaigns.
  • P2P Events: structured, time-bound fundraising programs such as walks, runs, rides, climbs, workplace challenges, and recurring event series.

DIY creates the product foundation. Events extends it with registration, teams and captains, event operations, participant communication, attribution, reporting, and integrations. The two directions must work as one coherent product while serving different customer workflows and levels of complexity.

About the Role

We are looking for a Product Manager to own P2P Events within the broader Peer-to-Peer product line.

This is a hands-on software product role covering discovery, definition, delivery, launch, and iteration. You will turn an ambiguous product area into a focused solution grounded in customer, usage, and commercial evidence.

Events and DIY serve different sides of the same system: nonprofits need to run fundraising programs, while participants need effective tools to fundraise. You will work closely with the PM responsible for the broader P2P area so these experiences and their shared capabilities evolve together.

This is not an event-planning or project-coordination role.

What You’ll Own

Define the product direction

  • Turn customer research, market evidence, and business context into a clear product thesis and sequenced roadmap.
  • Choose a focused target segment and event scenario rather than trying to serve the entire category at once.
  • Decide which capabilities belong in the shared P2P foundation and which require an Events-specific model.
  • Keep assumptions, success metrics, scope, risks, and product decisions explicit.

Lead discovery and product definition

  • Work directly with nonprofit event teams, participants, design partners, and internal GTM teams.
  • Validate decisions through interviews, workflow mapping, prototypes, and live product usage.
  • Separate true adoption blockers from feature requests and incumbent-product expectations.
  • Shape problems such as registration, teams and captains, attribution and reporting, event operations, participant communication, and CRM integrations. These are examples—not a pre-committed feature checklist.

Shape and deliver the product

  • Own the product from problem definition through requirements, delivery, launch, and iteration.
  • Write clear requirements, acceptance criteria, edge cases, and decision records.
  • Make day-to-day scope and trade-off decisions with Engineering, Design, Analytics, Research, and QA.
  • Ensure the product can evolve from simpler events to more advanced team structures, event series, and operational workflows without overbuilding the first release.
  • Keep delivery predictable by surfacing dependencies, risks, and unresolved decisions early.

Launch, learn, and drive outcomes

  • Launch and learn through EAPs with clear entry criteria, success measures, readiness requirements, and out-of-scope areas.
  • Understand whether organizations can run events successfully and whether participants activate, fundraise, and return.
  • Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, CSM, and Support on positioning, customer commitments, enablement, and competitive context.
  • Connect product evidence to adoption, expansion, pipeline, retention, and GPV.
  • Turn evidence into clear recommendations: iterate, expand, change direction, or stop.

Work AI-native

  • Use AI for research synthesis, prototyping, specification quality, data exploration, and operational automation.
  • Build testable artifacts quickly without outsourcing product judgment.

Requirements

  • 4–7 years of Product Management or Product Ownership experience in a software product company.
  • End-to-end ownership of a customer-facing product area with Engineering and Design.
  • Strong judgment in reducing a large problem space to a focused release and explaining the trade-offs.
  • Experience turning customer evidence and product data into decisions.
  • Clear written communication across requirements, edge cases, metrics, and decision records.
  • Ability to work with multi-actor workflows, permissions, states, and data relationships.
  • High ownership and independence, with fluent written and spoken English.

Strong plus

  • Experience with B2B SaaS, fundraising, payments, registration, events, community, or other multi-sided products.
  • Experience launching a new product area through beta or EAP.
  • Knowledge of CRM integrations, reporting, transaction attribution, analytics, or SQL.
  • Practical use of AI for research, prototyping, analysis, or product operations.

This Role May Not Be a Fit If

  • You are looking for an event-planning or internal project-management role rather than software product ownership.
  • You prefer to receive a fully defined roadmap and requirements instead of helping determine what should be built.
  • You want to work only on strategy and avoid specifications, QA, delivery details, or post-launch iteration.
  • You treat every customer request as a roadmap commitment.
  • You need stable scope and certainty before moving forward.
  • You measure progress mainly by features shipped rather than customer and business outcomes.

Why work with us

  • A strong, collaborative product team that owns what it builds
  • Clear product vision and access to real customer feedback from global nonprofit leaders
  • Flat structure: no politics, just great work with great people
  • Transparent company culture-we share how we’re growing, where revenue comes from, and what’s next
  • Long-term focus: we offer equity options and value sustained, meaningful contribution

Highlights:

About Fundraise Up

We’re Fundraise Up - a global fundraising platform built to make donating to nonprofits fast, seamless, and accessible to all. Every month, our technology powers tens of millions of dollars in donations across the globe. We focus on innovation that directly impacts results: faster load times, higher conversion rates, global payment support, and accessibility-first design.

Our platform is trusted by many of the world’s leading nonprofits, including UNICEF, the Alzheimer’s Association, and a wide range of global NGOs. With a 4.9/5 rating across top software review platforms, we’re recognized not just for our impact - but for the quality of the product we deliver.

A Truly Global Product

We operate in the enterprise segment, serving nonprofit organizations across North America, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Europe.

We’re building a large and complex product ecosystem that serves nonprofits, donors, and partners around the world. The platform includes a modern checkout experience and customizable widgets (each a standalone SPA), donor, organization, and partner portals, admin tools, and several internal apps.

The Team

We are a distributed team of 160+ product professionals. Our team members are mainly based across Spain, Poland, Portugal, Georgia, Armenia, Serbia, Turkey, and Cyprus.

Despite our scale, we operate like a focused team - where every task matters and every voice is heard. We value thoughtful collaboration, strong engineering practices, and a product mindset. You’ll be joining a team where quality, mentorship, and mutual respect come first.

About Peer-to-Peer at Fundraise Up

Peer-to-Peer turns supporters into fundraisers. Instead of only donating, a supporter creates a fundraising page, invites others to give, joins a team, or participates in an event on behalf of a nonprofit.

We are building Peer-to-Peer as a new product line. The product starts with two connected directions:

  • P2P DIY: self-serve fundraising for birthdays, memorials, personal challenges, and other supporter-led campaigns.
  • P2P Events: structured, time-bound fundraising programs such as walks, runs, rides, climbs, workplace challenges, and recurring event series.

DIY creates the product foundation. Events extends it with registration, teams and captains, event operations, participant communication, attribution, reporting, and integrations. The two directions must work as one coherent product while serving different customer workflows and levels of complexity.

About the Role

We are looking for a Product Manager to own P2P Events within the broader Peer-to-Peer product line.

This is a hands-on software product role covering discovery, definition, delivery, launch, and iteration. You will turn an ambiguous product area into a focused solution grounded in customer, usage, and commercial evidence.

Events and DIY serve different sides of the same system: nonprofits need to run fundraising programs, while participants need effective tools to fundraise. You will work closely with the PM responsible for the broader P2P area so these experiences and their shared capabilities evolve together.

This is not an event-planning or project-coordination role.

What You’ll Own

Define the product direction

  • Turn customer research, market evidence, and business context into a clear product thesis and sequenced roadmap.
  • Choose a focused target segment and event scenario rather than trying to serve the entire category at once.
  • Decide which capabilities belong in the shared P2P foundation and which require an Events-specific model.
  • Keep assumptions, success metrics, scope, risks, and product decisions explicit.

Lead discovery and product definition

  • Work directly with nonprofit event teams, participants, design partners, and internal GTM teams.
  • Validate decisions through interviews, workflow mapping, prototypes, and live product usage.
  • Separate true adoption blockers from feature requests and incumbent-product expectations.
  • Shape problems such as registration, teams and captains, attribution and reporting, event operations, participant communication, and CRM integrations. These are examples—not a pre-committed feature checklist.

Shape and deliver the product

  • Own the product from problem definition through requirements, delivery, launch, and iteration.
  • Write clear requirements, acceptance criteria, edge cases, and decision records.
  • Make day-to-day scope and trade-off decisions with Engineering, Design, Analytics, Research, and QA.
  • Ensure the product can evolve from simpler events to more advanced team structures, event series, and operational workflows without overbuilding the first release.
  • Keep delivery predictable by surfacing dependencies, risks, and unresolved decisions early.

Launch, learn, and drive outcomes

  • Launch and learn through EAPs with clear entry criteria, success measures, readiness requirements, and out-of-scope areas.
  • Understand whether organizations can run events successfully and whether participants activate, fundraise, and return.
  • Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, CSM, and Support on positioning, customer commitments, enablement, and competitive context.
  • Connect product evidence to adoption, expansion, pipeline, retention, and GPV.
  • Turn evidence into clear recommendations: iterate, expand, change direction, or stop.

Work AI-native

  • Use AI for research synthesis, prototyping, specification quality, data exploration, and operational automation.
  • Build testable artifacts quickly without outsourcing product judgment.

Requirements

  • 4–7 years of Product Management or Product Ownership experience in a software product company.
  • End-to-end ownership of a customer-facing product area with Engineering and Design.
  • Strong judgment in reducing a large problem space to a focused release and explaining the trade-offs.
  • Experience turning customer evidence and product data into decisions.
  • Clear written communication across requirements, edge cases, metrics, and decision records.
  • Ability to work with multi-actor workflows, permissions, states, and data relationships.
  • High ownership and independence, with fluent written and spoken English.

Strong plus

  • Experience with B2B SaaS, fundraising, payments, registration, events, community, or other multi-sided products.
  • Experience launching a new product area through beta or EAP.
  • Knowledge of CRM integrations, reporting, transaction attribution, analytics, or SQL.
  • Practical use of AI for research, prototyping, analysis, or product operations.

This Role May Not Be a Fit If

  • You are looking for an event-planning or internal project-management role rather than software product ownership.
  • You prefer to receive a fully defined roadmap and requirements instead of helping determine what should be built.
  • You want to work only on strategy and avoid specifications, QA, delivery details, or post-launch iteration.
  • You treat every customer request as a roadmap commitment.
  • You need stable scope and certainty before moving forward.
  • You measure progress mainly by features shipped rather than customer and business outcomes.

Why work with us

  • A strong, collaborative product team that owns what it builds
  • Clear product vision and access to real customer feedback from global nonprofit leaders
  • Flat structure: no politics, just great work with great people
  • Transparent company culture-we share how we’re growing, where revenue comes from, and what’s next
  • Long-term focus: we offer equity options and value sustained, meaningful contribution

jobs.excerpt: The Executive Director, Pharmacovigilance (PV) is a senior individual contributor and team leader who will serve as a cornerstone of the company's global drug safety function.
jobs.description:
The Executive Director, Pharmacovigilance (PV) is a senior individual contributor and team leader who will serve as a cornerstone of the company's global drug safety function. This role has end-to-end accountability for pharmacovigilance activities supporting late-phase clinical development and regulatory submissions for the company's biologic pipeline. The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in global safety surveillance, aggregate safety reporting, and the preparation of integrated safety documents required for BLA and MAA filings, and will thrive in a fast-paced, resource-lean biotech environment where initiative and scientific rigor are equally valued.

Duties and Responsibilities (Include but are not limited to):

Late-Phase Global Pharmacovigilance Operations
  • Lead and execute all PV activities for Phase 3 and registrational biologics programs, ensuring full compliance with ICH E2A, E2B, E2C, E2D, and E2E guidelines, as well as FDA, EMA, and other applicable regional requirements.
  • Oversee global signal detection, evaluation, and management activities, including Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) coding review and benefit-risk assessment updates.
  • Manage and optimize safety data receipt, processing, and reporting workflows, including collaboration with CROs, data management teams, and clinical operations.
  • Serve as the subject-matter expert and primary PV point of contact for cross-functional clinical teams, regulatory affairs, and medical affairs.
  • Maintain and enforce the company's global safety database and adverse event reporting infrastructure, including oversight of vendor relationships.
Aggregate Safety Reporting & Regulatory Submissions
  • Author and/or oversee the preparation of Integrated Safety Summaries (ISS) and Integrated Summaries of Efficacy (ISE) for BLA and MAA submissions (member of the submission team), ensuring scientific rigor, internal consistency, and full alignment with regulatory expectations (21 CFR 314.50, Module 2.7.4, ICH E3, ICH M4E).
  • Oversaw end-to-end safety labeling strategy for biologics, ensuring compliance with FDA, EMA, and other global regulatory requirements for products with boxed warnings, REMS, restricted access programs, and other post-marketing risk mitigation obligations.
  • Lead the development of Clinical Study Report (CSR) safety sections for Phase 2 and Phase 3 studies, including narrative writing, adverse event tabulations, and laboratory data analyses.
  • Prepare and manage Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSURs), Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Reports (PBRERs), and Development Safety Update Reports (DSURs) on global schedules.
  • Prepare Risk Management Plans (RMPs) and Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS), including strategy development and execution.
  • Respond to health authority questions and requests for safety information during regulatory review processes (e.g., Complete Response Letters, Day 120/180 questions).
Safety Surveillance & Pharmacoepidemiology
  • Design and implement systematic pharmacovigilance surveillance programs, including benefit-risk monitoring frameworks and safety monitoring plans for clinical trials.
  • Conduct and document ongoing signal detection activities; prepare signal assessment reports and escalate findings to the Safety Monitoring Committee and/or Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) as appropriate.
  • Collaborate with clinical pharmacology and biostatistics teams to interpret safety trends across populations and study designs.
  • Support post-marketing commitments and Phase 4 safety studies, including protocol development and safety monitoring plan creation.
Cross-Functional Leadership & PV Infrastructure
  • Partner with Clinical and Regulatory Affairs to define global filing strategy and PV regulatory timelines; represent the PV function in Health Authority meetings and advisory committee preparations.
  • Collaborate with Medical Affairs and Commercial teams on labeling updates, healthcare professional communications, and post-approval safety activities.
  • Build, mentor, and manage a small PV team (or oversee contract resources) as the company scales; establish and maintain SOPs, work instructions, and quality standards.
  • Evaluate, select, and manage CRO/vendor partnerships for pharmacovigilance services; conduct oversight audits and ensure GVP compliance.
  • Represent PV on the Clinical Development Team (CDT) and participate in Program Team leadership meetings.
Supervisory Responsibilities:
This position does not have supervisory responsibilities at this time. Supervisory responsibilities may be added at a future date.

Education/Experience/Skills:
  • Doctor of Medicine (MD) degree from an accredited institution is required.
  • 12+ years of progressive pharmaceutical/biotech industry pharmacovigilance experience, with at least 5 years in a senior role with direct accountability for late-phase global biologics PV programs.
  • Demonstrated hands-on authorship of Integrated Safety Summaries (ISS) submitted in at least one BLA or MAA; experience with multiple submissions strongly preferred.
  • Extensive experience authoring CSR safety sections, DSURs, and PSURs/PBRERs for biologic compounds in global development.
  • Deep command of ICH guidelines (E2A–E2E, E6, E8, M4E), FDA/CDER and EMA/EMA GVP Module requirements, and regional pharmacovigilance regulations (EU, US, Japan, and other ICH regions).
  • Extensive experience with signal detection methodologies, benefit-risk assessment frameworks, and safety narrative writing.
  • Proven track record managing CRO/vendor PV relationships and safety database oversight (Argus, ARISg, or equivalent).
  • Experience in small biotech or start-up environments is desired; comfortable operating with limited infrastructure and high personal accountability.
  • Experience with BLA or MAA approval for a biologic; post-approval PV experience a plus.
  • Familiarity with rare disease, orphan drug, or first-in-class biologic programs.
  • Experience presenting to Health Authorities (FDA, EMA) and participation in Advisory Committee proceedings.
  • Familiarity with REMS design and implementation or EU RMP preparation.
  • Knowledge of pharmacoepidemiology methodologies and real-world evidence applications in safety assessment.
  • Exceptional scientific and medical writing ability; proven capacity to synthesize complex safety data into clear, structured regulatory documents under tight timelines.
  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills; ability to independently evaluate complex safety signals and formulate evidence-based recommendations.
  • High scientific credibility with the ability to engage and challenge clinical, statistical, and regulatory colleagues at a peer level.
  • Excellent project management skills; able to manage multiple competing priorities without sacrificing quality.
  • Demonstrated leadership and cross-functional collaboration is crucial.
Physical Demands:
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to walk, stand, and sit. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds.

Working Environment and Travel:
Home office working environment.
Domestic and International business related to travel (estimated 10–20%). Travel will include team meetings, interactions with the Health Authorities, investigator meetings, and conference participation.

Overview

EV Infrastructure Project Manager – Remote - US

NV5 provides end-to-end services to fleet and property owners with their clean transportation transition. We plan, design, and manage zero-emission infrastructure and vehicle projects for schools, white fleets, and medium to heavy-duty applications.

Our unique expertise includes technical knowledge, energy and financial expertise, and market insight. This broad understanding of Electric Vehicles (EVs), Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE), and energy results in sophisticated transition strategy for fleets and infrastructure. We also maintain a close watch on the clean transportation market, actively engaging with vehicle manufacturers, EVSE suppliers and charge management software (CMS) providers on behalf of clients.

With hundreds of EVSE design projects completed, NV5 provides full EVSE design services and ongoing owner’s representative support for construction and operation.

We are seeking a Project Manager that will lead EV Infrastructure projects nationwide, primarily California. In this role you will lead the pre-development and development phases of projects from feasibility through permitting and construction.

Our Technical Project Managers at this level are responsible for planning, scheduling, and coordinating with project teams to execute detailed phases of the engineering and design work.

You will be the primary contact for clients, contractors, and other professionals, serving as a project leader and is expected to effectively coordinate the team’s work to ensure the highest quality product is on time and on budget.

Responsibilities

Other responsibilities include:

  • Project Lifecycle Management. Lead all phases of EV and renewable energy project development, including design oversight, procurement, construction, and commissioning
  • Provide project management to lead the civil, electrical, and structural engineering teams in the delivery of EV/EVSE infrastructure including planning, design, commissioning, and consulting on complex projects.
  • Demonstrate strong electric vehicle charging experience including feasibility assessment and cost estimating.
  • Collaborate across verticals and supporting teams to enable smooth project phase transitions.
  • Working knowledge of other renewable technologies that may be integrated into projects such as battery energy storage systems (BESS), Microgrids, and Solar PV.
  • Proactive, coordination of engineering and design activities to comply with budgets and schedules; identify departures or issues early to meet client expectations for project excellence, budget, and schedule.
  • Coordinate with engineering and drafting teams.
  • Participate in training project staff, as appropriate.
  • Provide overall package quality assurance checks on deliverables. Note that each engineering discipline is responsible for technical quality assurance and quality control.
  • Participate in business development activities including preparation of proposals for new work.
  • Develop and maintain client relationships.
  • Analyze and solve operational problems by leveraging tools such as Smartsheet.
  • May prepare addendums, proposal requests and change orders; initiate additional service requests and coordinate with the team to collect applicable information for client submittal.
  • May prepare Schedule of Values (SOV) or Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimates at various stages of the EV charging, solar and BESS projects.
  • Interpret and apply client, company, and project requirements, as needed.

Qualifications

We are seeking the following experience & qualifications:

  • B.S. Degree in relevant field, such as General Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Project Management, or Construction Management.
  • M.S. Degree in relevant field such as General Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Business Administration is a plus.
  • PMP certification preferred.
  • Experience in budgeting, scheduling, planning EV/EVSE, solar and projects.
  • Experience using Primavera P6 or Microsoft Project scheduling software.
  • 5+ years’ project experience within electric vehicle (EV) infrastructure and EV supply equipment (EVSE), preferably with Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) and solar and/or BESS project experience.
  • 10+ years’ of Project Management experience leading multi-disciplinary teams in planning, cost estimating, engineering and design, survey, permitting, construction, and utility coordination on complex multi-site projects for local and national clients.
  • Knowledge of Edge Computing is a plus.

jobs.description:
Background

The Condominium Authority of Ontario (CAO) is a dynamic, digital organization that supports the province's rapidly evolving condominium sector with information, education and dispute resolution services.

The CAO is a delegated administrative authority that supports condo living and enhances consumer protection by providing services and resources that reach all condo communities across Ontario. We are accountable to the government through an Administrative Agreement with the Minister of Public and Business Service Delivery and Procurement. The seven-member board of directors provide strategic guidance and oversight of the organization.

We are an organization driven by our vision, mission and values:

Our Vision: Strong and vibrant condominium communities in Ontario.

Our Mission: Engage and empower Ontario’s condominium communities with information, education, and dispute resolution

Corporate Values: Innovation, trust, teamwork, value for money, integrity, fairness

Team Values: Respect, trust, diversity, collaboration, leadership

Role Purpose

The Condominium Authority of Ontario is seeking a Mediation Services Coordinator to support the implementation and administration of its Community Mediation Pilot Program.

The pilot program is designed to assess the effectiveness of community-based mediation services in helping condominium communities resolve disputes constructively and efficiently. The successful candidate will play a key role in coordinating program operations, supporting volunteer mediators, maintaining case administration processes, and ensuring the timely progression of mediation files.

Reporting to the Director, Policy, Programs & Dispute Resolution, the Mediation Services Coordinator (the "Coordinator") is responsible for the administration, coordination, and operational delivery of the CAO Community Mediation Pilot Program. The Coordinator serves as the central point of contact for applicants, volunteer mediators, and participating parties, supporting intake, eligibility screening, case assignment, scheduling, stakeholder communications, records management, and program evaluation activities.

The Coordinator plays a critical role in ensuring that mediation files progress efficiently, stakeholders receive timely support, and pilot outcomes are accurately tracked and reported.

Key Responsibilities

Program Administration & Intake

  • Respond to inquiries regarding the Community Mediation Pilot Program.
  • Provide information to prospective applicants, participants, and other stakeholders regarding program processes and eligibility requirements. Coordinate intake activities and support case administration throughout the mediation process.
  • Conduct preliminary eligibility screening in accordance with approved program criteria and procedures.

Case Coordination

  • Assign cases to co-mediation teams based on availability, capacity, and other operational considerations
  • Coordinate scheduling and administrative logistics for mediators and participants
  • Monitor case progress and support the timely completion of mediation activities.
  • Identify operational issues and escalate matters as appropriate.

Stakeholder Support

  • Serve as the primary contact for volunteer mediators participating in the pilot.
  • Maintain regular communication with applicants, mediation participants, volunteer mediators, and other stakeholders.
  • Support a positive participant experience through timely, professional, and responsive service.

Records, Reporting & Evaluation

  • Maintain accurate and confidential case files, records, and program documentation.
  • Ensure the accurate collection and maintenance of program data, metrics, and statistical information.
  • Support participant feedback collection and pilot evaluation activities.
  • Prepare reports, summaries, and updates regarding program activity and outcomes.
  • Assist with the development and continuous improvement of program procedures, tools, and resources.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to enhance service delivery and administrative efficiency.
  • Contribute recommendations regarding pilot design, operational processes, and future program implementation.

Qualifications, Skills & Knowledge

Required

  • Post-secondary education in a relevant field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Demonstrated experience providing administrative, program coordination, or case management support.
  • Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and competing deadlines.
  • Strong interpersonal and communications skills, both written and verbal.
  • Demonstrated commitment to professionalism, discretion, and confidentiality when managing sensitive information.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and virtual meeting platforms.
  • Strong customer service and stakeholder management skills.

Assets

  • Experience in mediation, dispute resolution, alternative dispute resolution (ADR), or community-based conflict resolution.
  • Mediation training, certification, or postgraduate education related to dispute resolution.
  • Experience supporting volunteer-based programs or initiatives.
  • Experience in project coordination, program administration, or case management.
  • Knowledge of Ontario’s condominium sector and condominium governance.
  • Experience working within a regulatory, public-sector, tribunal, or not-for-profit environment.

Compensation & Engagement terms

  • Six-month independent contractor engagement.
  • Hourly rate of $30-38 per hour, with invoices submitted and paid on a bi-weekly basis.
  • Full-time anticipated workload during the engagement period.
  • Fully remote work arrangement, with occasional attendance at meetings as required.
  • Contractor will be responsible for own applicable statutory remittances, insurance, and business expenses unless otherwise agreed to in advance.
  • The CAO or the Contractor may terminate the engagement at any time by providing two (2) weeks’ written notice.

How to Apply

Interested candidates are invited to submit a resume and an optional cover letter no later than October 2, 2026 at 9:00am EST.

The Condominium Authority of Ontario is committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace and welcomes applications from all qualified individuals.

Accommodation is available upon request throughout the recruitment process. Applicants requiring accommodation are encouraged to notify us at any stage of the selection process.

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Digitial Transformation Partner (P&C)
jobs.excerpt: WELL Health Technologies is an innovative technology-enabled healthcare company whose overarching objective is to positively impact health outcomes by leveraging technology to empower and support healthcare practitioners and their patients.
jobs.description:
WELL Health Technologies is an innovative technology-enabled healthcare company whose overarching objective is to positively impact health outcomes by leveraging technology to empower and support healthcare practitioners and their patients.

WELL has built an innovative practitioner enablement platform that includes comprehensive end to end practice management tools inclusive of virtual care and digital patient engagement capabilities as well as Electronic Medical Records (EMR), Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) and data protection services. WELL Health Technologies, uses this platform to power healthcare practitioners both inside and outside of WELL Health Technologies’ own omni-channel patient services offerings.

WELL owns and operates Canada's largest network of outpatient medical clinics serving primary and specialized healthcare services and is the provider of a leading multi-national multi-disciplinary telehealth offering. WELL Health Technologies is publicly traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol "WELL".

To learn more about the company, please visit: .


The opportunity

Reporting to the VP, Business Transformation, we are hiring a Digital Transformation Partner (People & Culture) to help shape and deliver WELL Health’s digital and AI agenda across People & Culture. In this newly created role, you will work closely with P&C leaders and teams to understand how work gets done today, identify pain points and opportunities, and determine where AI, automation, and technology can simplify processes, improve the employee experience, and create measurable value.

This is a hands-on role where you will take opportunities from discovery through implementation and adoption. You will map processes, define requirements, prioritize use cases, and design and build automations, AI agents, and workflows. For more complex solutions, you will partner with WELL’s AI, Data, and enterprise technology teams while continuing to own the business outcome.

Your scope will span the employee lifecycle, including hiring, onboarding, payroll, total rewards, employee programs, M&A, and broader strategic initiatives. As WELL continues to grow, you will help P&C build its digital and AI capabilities while creating scalable solutions and approaches that can evolve with the organization.

This is a fully remote role based anywhere in Canada, with a preference for candidates located in Vancouver.

Who you are

You are a hands-on digital transformation professional who enjoys turning business challenges into practical solutions people actually use. You can move from a conversation about a frustrating process or recurring pain point to understanding the underlying problem, identifying where technology can make a difference, and building and implementing a solution.

You bring together technical capability, business thinking, and curiosity. You are comfortable building with AI and automation tools yourself, while knowing when a solution requires deeper data, AI, or engineering expertise. You can navigate ambiguity, ask the right questions, prioritize opportunities based on value and complexity, and take ownership from discovery and design through testing, deployment, and adoption.

You are equally comfortable working with technology and people. You can partner with senior People & Culture leaders, understand the realities of how teams work, and translate between business needs and technical possibilities. Most importantly, you are motivated by outcomes: simplifying work, improving the employee experience, and helping teams confidently adopt new ways of working.

What's in it for you

Build and see your work in action. You will have the opportunity to take real P&C challenges from an initial pain point through to a working solution. Rather than stopping at strategy or recommendations, you will build, test, deploy, and improve AI agents, automations, and workflows that simplify how work gets done and create measurable value for employees and the P&C team.

Ownership and influence. As a newly created role embedded in People & Culture, you will have direct access to senior P&C leaders and the autonomy to help identify and prioritize where digital transformation can have the greatest impact. You will influence the roadmap while owning selected initiatives from discovery through implementation and adoption.

Broad scope and technical growth. You will work across hiring, onboarding, payroll, total rewards, employee programs, M&A, and larger strategic initiatives, giving you exposure to a wide range of business challenges. You will also partner with WELL’s AI, Data, and technology teams and work with evolving AI and automation capabilities, expanding both your technical expertise and your understanding of enterprise transformation.

Help shape what comes next. You will join WELL as it continues to build its digital transformation capabilities and explore how AI can improve work across the organization. As an early member of the Digital Transformation Partner team, you will have the opportunity to help establish approaches and practices that can be applied beyond P&C as the function grows.

You will:

  • You will build and see your work in action. You will take real P&C challenges from an initial pain point through to a working solution. You will build, test, deploy, and improve AI agents, automations, and workflows that simplify how work gets done and create measurable value for employees and the P&C team.
  • You will have ownership and influence. You will have direct access to senior P&C leaders and the autonomy to help identify and prioritize where digital transformation can have the greatest impact. You will influence the roadmap while owning selected initiatives from discovery and design through implementation and adoption.
  • You will broaden your scope and technical expertise. You will work across hiring, onboarding, payroll, total rewards, employee programs, M&A, and larger strategic initiatives. You will partner with WELL’s AI, Data, and technology teams, gaining exposure to evolving AI and automation capabilities while deepening your experience delivering enterprise transformation.
  • You will help shape what comes next. You will join WELL as it continues to build its digital transformation capabilities and explore how AI can improve work across the organization. As an early member of the Digital Transformation Partner team, you will help establish approaches and practices that can be applied beyond P&C as the function grows.

Here's what you bring:

  • The digital transformation experience. You have experience taking digital transformation, automation, AI, product, or technology-enabled initiatives from an identified business problem through to implementation and adoption. You can assess how work happens today, uncover opportunities for improvement, define a future state, and turn ideas into practical solutions that deliver measurable value.
  • The hands-on AI and automation skills. You have experience building and deploying AI-enabled solutions, automations, agents, or workflows. You are comfortable working with modern AI tools and understand what it takes to move beyond experimentation to solutions that are tested, reliable, secure, and useful in a business environment.
  • The business and process mindset. You can dig into an ambiguous or inefficient process, ask thoughtful questions, map requirements, and determine where technology can create the greatest value. You know how to balance business impact, complexity, available resources, and technical feasibility when prioritizing what to solve and how to solve it.
  • The technical toolkit. You have worked with tools and platforms used to build AI and automation solutions. Experience within the Microsoft ecosystem, including Copilot Studio, AI Foundry, or Fabric, is valuable, as is exposure to OpenAI or Anthropic technologies. Familiarity with HR platforms such as Workday, UKG, ADP, or Shareworks would be an asset.
  • The collaboration and communication skills. You can build trusted relationships with senior leaders, business stakeholders, and technical teams. You can translate business needs into clear technical requirements and explain technical possibilities in practical terms, bringing different perspectives together to move an initiative forward.
  • The ownership and adaptability. You are comfortable operating in a highly matrixed environment where priorities and requirements may evolve. You can bring structure to ambiguity, move between strategy and hands-on execution, and stay accountable for an initiative through testing, deployment, change management, and adoption.

Preferred qualifications

While not required, experience working with Microsoft technologies such as Fabric, AI Foundry, or Copilot Studio would be an asset. Additional experience with AI platforms such as OpenAI or Anthropic, as well as exposure to People & Culture processes or HR systems such as Workday, UKG, ADP, or Shareworks, would help you ramp up quickly. Experience applying AI and automation within People & Culture or other enterprise business functions is also considered an asset.


Why join us?

Healthcare is our sector, and we know that for WELL to be a winning team, we must provide an open environment to prioritize health and wellbeing and multiple resources to discuss mental, physical, and psychological needs openly. From the CEO to the newest hire, everyone comes together as part of our culture of respect, openness, support, and communication. We unite to empower each other to be the best we can be.

We recognize that the best way to serve our diverse patient communities is by reflecting that diversity. With almost 65% of our team members identifying as female and 70% of our leadership identifying as a visible minority, we are proud of our diverse, equitable and inclusive organization.


Apply now

Interested in applying but worried you don't have it all? At WELL, we know not everyone gains their experience following a traditional path. If you share our values, want to make a difference in healthcare technology solutions, and meet 70% of the qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Express your interest here.

What you can expect from our interview process:

  • A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining WELL Health and in the role. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
  • A virtual interview with the Senior Director, Business Transformation to discuss your experience, technical depth, hands-on approach to AI and automation, and how you think about solving business challenges through digital transformation.
  • An interview with the Director, People & Culture and Chief People Officer to learn more about your understanding of People & Culture challenges, your approach to partnering with P&C leaders and teams, and how you would support WELL’s digital transformation agenda.
  • A final interview with the VP, Business Transformation to discuss WELL’s broader transformation agenda and growth strategy, and the role you will play in helping move these priorities forward.

Compensation

The salary range for this position is $130K- 150K plus bonuses. The salary will be determined based on several factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, skills, and the needs of the organization. At WELL, we are committed to fair and equitable compensation and aim to provide a competitive salary that reflects the value and expertise of the successful candidate.

WELL is committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and accessible workplace. We welcome and celebrate the diversity of applicants and team members across ability, race, gender identity, sexual orientation, and lived experience. We strive to create an environment where differences are valued and contribute to our collective success – this is the WELL Way.

WELL has been independently certified as a Great Place to Work® by the Great Place to Work Institute® Canada. This recognition reflects our commitment to building a workplace culture rooted in trust, inclusivity, and employee well-being. It also aligns with our Healthy Place to Work pillar and the priorities outlined in our annual Sustainability Impact Report.

jobs.description:
About the team

Zillow Closing helps make real estate closings faster, simpler, and more secure. Since 2016, our team has supported more than $20 billion in transactions nationwide by combining deep title and real estate expertise with product, technology, and operational innovation.

Our Title Solutions team is a small, high-impact group at the center of that work. We partner across Closing, search vendors, attorneys, underwriters, and other transaction stakeholders to solve complex title matters and create a more seamless experience for customers.

We believe the future of real estate is powered by automation, efficiency, and digital experiences. Our mission is to deliver the products and services that make those experiences possible—and to build a better closing journey for everyone involved.

About the role

Zillow Closing is looking for an experienced Title Officer to bring deep search, examination, and curative expertise to our Title Solutions team. You will independently manage title-only files through examination and curative, resolve complex title matters, and help deliver a world-class closing experience.

You will work closely with search vendors to obtain complete search packages, keep Closing Associates informed of file status, and maintain momentum across a fast-moving pipeline. Success in this role means combining technical judgment, urgency, clear communication, and meticulous attention to detail to meet our service-level commitments.

In this role, you will:

  • Review county records, search packages, tax certificates, tax assessor reports, attorney title opinions, surveys, and other property records to identify requirements and exceptions for title commitments.

  • Conduct and evaluate county, DataTrace, PACER, Patriot/OFAC, LexisNexis, and related searches.

  • Examine title commitments and attorney title opinions to identify matters that must be resolved before or at closing, including loans, liens, judgments, taxes, municipal liens, UCC terminations, and affidavit requirements.

  • Coordinate with consumers, creditors, attorneys, underwriters, and vendors to cure title issues efficiently and accurately.

  • Update title commitments as new information becomes available during clearance, including revising requirements and exceptions when a matter has been resolved.

  • Interpret buyer and lender waiver requests and prepare pro forma title policies or marked-up title commitments.

  • Draft or coordinate deeds, affidavits, escrow agreements, and other legal documents where permitted; review recorded instruments such as releases.

  • Review county GIS overlays and satellite imagery to identify potential survey needs.

  • Review and approve complex supporting documentation, including surveys, divorce decrees, trust agreements, probate records, bankruptcies, death certificates, entity formation documents, and court dockets.

  • Generate and revise Insured Closing Protection Letters and calculate title insurance premiums and invoices for title-only transactions.

  • Accurately enter clearance-related charges, such as survey invoices, into settlement statements.

  • Communicate clearly and proactively with all transaction parties by phone and email, including supporting the general phone line as needed.

  • Confirm all outstanding matters are cleared before or at close of escrow while effectively prioritizing a fast-moving queue of urgent work.

  • Meet established turnaround times, service standards, and quality metrics that are monitored and reported weekly.

This role has been categorized as a Remote position. “Remote” employees do not have a permanent corporate office workplace and, instead, work from a physical location of their choice, which must be identified to the Company. U.S. employees may live in any of the 50 United States, with limited exceptions.In California, Connecticut, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Washington state, and Washington DC the standard base pay range for this role is $30.20 - $45.20 hourly. This base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.In Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Minnesota, Nevada, Ohio, Rhode Island, Vermont, and Virginia the standard base pay range for this role is $28.60 - $43.00 hourly. The base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.In addition to a competitive base salary this position is also eligible for equity awards based on factors such as experience, performance and location. Actual amounts will vary depending on experience, performance and location. Employees in this role will not be paid below the salary threshold for exempt employees in the state where they reside.

Who you are

You are a detail-oriented title professional who takes pride in resolving complex issues, keeping commitments, and creating a high-quality experience for internal and external customers. You thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced environment and bring the judgment and initiative to move work forward independently.

You bring:

  • Eight or more years of title examination and curative experience within a title operation.

  • A four-year college degree.

  • Search, examination, and curative experience supporting transactions at a national scale.

  • Strong expertise in one or more of the following markets is preferred: Maryland, Virginia, Washington, DC, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, or New Jersey.

  • Deep knowledge of title search, examination, curative, and clearance practices, including ALTA title insurance forms, endorsements, issuing guidelines, metes-and-bounds legal descriptions, and common mortgage loan documents.

  • Confidence editing deeds, affidavits, indemnity agreements, and related documentation.

  • Proficiency with title production software and tools such as DataTrace, PACER, LexisNexis, Slack, and other search and examination platforms.

  • Exceptional attention to detail, sound judgment, and the ability to identify and resolve complex title issues.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to consult effectively with Closing teams, search vendors, underwriters, attorneys, and leaders on technical title matters.

  • The ability to manage multiple files and competing deadlines while maintaining a positive, collaborative approach and supporting teammates when needed.

  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, evolving environment where requirements, markets, and processes may change.

  • A proactive, resourceful problem-solving mindset: you see the bigger picture, investigate solutions, and know when to escalate.

If you thrive in complex title work, take pride in solving problems others cannot, and want to help build the future of closing, we’d love to hear from you.

Get to know us

At Zillow, we’re reimagining how people move—through the real estate market and through their careers. As the most-visited real estate platform in the U.S., we help customers navigate buying, selling, financing and renting with greater ease and confidence. Whether you're working in tech, sales, operations, or design, you’ll be part of a company that's reshaping an industry and helping more people make home a reality.

Zillow is honored to be recognized among the best workplaces in the country. Zillow was named one of FORTUNE 100 Best Companies to Work For® in 2025, and included on the PEOPLE Companies That Care® 2025list, reflecting our commitment to creating an innovative, inclusive, and engaging culture where employees are empowered to grow.

No matter where you sit in the organization, your work will help drive innovation, support our customers, and move the industry—and your career—forward, together.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please contact your recruiter directly.

Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with applicable state and local law.

jobs.title: AI Partner
jobs.excerpt: Convergent Research is a nonprofit science studio best known for pioneering the Focused Research Organization (FRO): purpose-built, mission-driven orgs designed to solve technological bottlenecks, unlock whole new fields, and lead to scaled revolutions.
jobs.description:
Convergent Research is a nonprofit science studio best known for pioneering the Focused Research Organization (FRO): purpose-built, mission-driven orgs designed to solve technological bottlenecks, unlock whole new fields, and lead to scaled revolutions. We’ve proven our model works by building over 14 high-impact scientific organizations spanning AI, biotech, mathematics, climate science, and more.
AI capability is compounding faster than the world's ability to absorb it. Other technologies got decades to sort out their safety codes, their testing regimes, and the institutions that enforce them. We don't have decades. The defenses have to be built while the technology is still moving, and there's no budget line anywhere that says build the defenses now.
That's the gap this role exists to close. Not "how do we build another AI company" — plenty of people are doing that. This role is about building the missing institutions and technical infrastructure that make the world resilient to advanced AI: the defensive capabilities that won't be built by a startup, won't fit inside an academic lab, and are too important to leave to chance.

What you’ll do

    Partners at Convergent are like senior partners at a venture incubator. You'll create and fully own a growing portfolio of FROs and other scientific projects that advance AI resilience — society's capacity to capture AI's benefits while withstanding its risks.
    The portfolio is yours to define, but the surface area is much bigger than model safety alone. It spans defensive biosecurity (pathogen-agnostic detection, next-generation PPE, rapid countermeasures), provably secure cyber-physical systems and formal verification, epistemic infrastructure for a world flooded with AI-generated content, independent evaluation and monitoring capacity, compute governance, economic modeling of the transition — and areas nobody has named yet. The unifying question: what keystone defensive capability, if it existed, would make the world meaningfully harder to break?
    You will have extreme latitude to decide what your portfolio should include, and the resources to go build it.
    You’ll form strong theses, find extraordinary founders, pressure-test ideas, raise money, build boards, launch organizations, and help them move with the speed and focus of the best deep-tech startups.

    Specifically, you will:

  • Roadmap the AI resilience landscape to identify the bottlenecks and keystone capabilities worth building organizations around

  • Source and diligence ideas for new projects and organizations and design funding calls in partnership with funders

  • Build founding teams and help recruit the early hires who will make or break them

  • Directly contribute to and coach founders on technical and organizational roadmaps, fundraising, and standing up startup ops from zero

  • Serve as a Director on multiple FRO boards, keeping teams on track against milestones and helping founders make the genuinely hard calls on funding, strategic direction, hiring, firing, and operations

  • Represent Convergent externally, building high-trust relationships with the philanthropic and public funders now committing serious capital to AI resilience

  • Contribute to Convergent-wide initiatives like our Founder Retreats and Residencies

Who you are

  • You understand the AI landscape of 2026 in granular detail: who is building what, why, and on what timeline

  • More importantly, you have a view on where that leaves the rest of the world exposed, and which of those exposures are tractable and through what clever ideas and technical methods they might be patchable, and who are the people developing those ideas

  • You have ideas, or a credible plan to find ideas, for large-scale efforts that would measurably improve how the world weathers this transition

  • You can argue passionately for a thesis about where philanthropic capital should go, and then argue the other side just as well

  • You're technically fluent in frontier AI, enough to tell a real bottleneck from a fashionable one

  • You have a deep network in the field and people pick up when you call

  • You know how startups actually work, probably because you’ve worked at one, or at a venture firm, or built something yourself

  • You’ve raised money, owned a budget, written technical roadmaps, and hired people

  • You’ve assembled a group of people to do a hard technical thing, and it worked

  • You’ve spent time around boards, governance, or nonprofit leadership

  • You communicate clearly and you move fast

    • It’s okay if you don’t meet every single criterion above perfectly.If you've read this far, and you're already sketching the organization you'd build first, we want to hear from you.

In 6 months you will have

  • Written a clear thesis for Convergent’s AI resilience portfolio: the areas we should pursue, the bottlenecks we are uniquely positioned to unlock, and the kinds of founders we should be backing.

  • Helped at least one promising founder or founding team move from early concept toward a fundable, technically credible organizational plan.

  • Built a strong map of the AI resilience ecosystem, including researchers, funders, labs, nonprofits, policymakers, and technical experts whose work should inform our portfolio.

  • Sourced and diligenced a serious pipeline of potential FROs or FRO-like projects, with several ready for deeper development

  • Built trusted relationships with key funders and external advisors who can help us launch ambitious new AI resilience institutions.

What you’ll get

  • A rare chance to build institutional architecture for frontier science alongside some of the sharpest people working across a dozen fields

  • Competitive salary, with a range of $200,000 - $350,000.

  • Up to a 6% 401k match because future-you deserves comfort

  • Top-tier medical, dental, and vision insurance—majority of options are fully covered for you and your dependents. Stay healthy, my friend

  • Company-paid life insurance, AD&D, long- and short-term disability insurance, as well as voluntary supplemental insurance options

  • 19 holidays (including a full week off at the end of the year—yes, we enforce it)

  • 3 weeks PTO with tenure increases, with separate allotments for sick and parental leave

  • Generous fertility benefits and childcare reimbursement—because tiny humans are a big deal

  • Education and professional development benefits

  • Wellness allowance for fitness and wellness activities (treat yourself to climbing shoes or Calm.com—no judgment)

  • 3x/year offsite team retreats and additional opportunities to meet your teammates in person

Convergent Research exists to fill a structural gap in the R&D system. We enable fundamental research that requires unusual levels of scale and coordination yet is not rapidly monetizable by industry. We’re bringing together top talent from academia, industry, and startups to build a new model for innovative R&D.
We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive. We believe in hiring individuals based on their unique talents—not on race, color, religion, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law or our company policies. We are more than a proud Equal Employment Opportunity employer. Our goal is to foster a healthy, safe, and respectful environment where all employees are valued and treated with dignity. Harassment of any kind is not tolerated here.

This role suits someone who lives and breathes infrastructure-as-code, treats automation as the default way of working, and wants to deliver resilient, secure and cost-efficient cloud platforms for our customers.

What you'll be doing

You'll design, build and maintain Azure infrastructure using Terraform as the primary IaC (infrastructure-as-code) tool, working to modular, reusable and version-controlled patterns. You'll develop and own CI/CD pipelines across Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions for both infrastructure and application deployments, and automate provisioning, configuration and lifecycle management across multiple client environments and subscriptions.

You'll implement and enforce security, governance and compliance baselines, covering Azure Policy, RBAC (role-based access control), Key Vault, networking and landing zones, and you'll monitor, troubleshoot and optimise the performance, reliability and cost of Azure workloads. As the senior technical escalation point for Azure, Terraform and DevOps practices, you'll coordinate workload and prioritisation across the team, conduct code and architecture reviews, and help uphold engineering excellence across the team's output.

You'll work closely with Solution Architects and the Head of Cloud Operations on solution design, migrations and customer onboarding, and you'll take part in an on-call / out-of-hours rota.

What you'll bring

You'll have proven, in-depth experience engineering and operating Microsoft Azure environments in production, along with extensive Terraform experience - writing, structuring and maintaining modules, state management, workspaces and remote backends. You'll bring a strong DevOps background, including CI/CD pipeline design, Git-based workflows and release automation.

You'll have demonstrable experience leading or mentoring engineers, setting technical direction and coordinating team delivery, plus solid scripting ability in PowerShell, Bash or Python. A sound understanding of Azure networking, identity (Entra ID), security and governance is essential, alongside experience with monitoring and observability tooling such as Azure Monitor and Log Analytics. You'll bring excellent troubleshooting skills and a methodical, root-cause approach to problems.

It would also be great if you had

Azure certifications (such as AZ-104, AZ-305 or AZ-400) or a HashiCorp Terraform Associate qualification, experience with containers and orchestration (AKS, Docker, Kubernetes), exposure to multi-tenant or MSP environments and client-facing delivery, and familiarity with configuration management and policy-as-code tooling.

What we offer

You'll join a skilled, collaborative Cloud Operations team working on varied, high-impact projects, with genuine investment in your growth through funded certifications and training. We offer flexible, fully remote working from anywhere in the UK, and a culture that values automation, engineering excellence and continuous improvement.

Let's connect. Let's grow.

LexisNexis Legal & Professional, which serves customers in more than 150 countries with 11,800 employees worldwide, is part of RELX ( a global provider of information-based analytics and decision tools for professional and business customers. You will collaborate with editorial, technology, and commercial teams while working with AI-enabled tools and workflows to support innovative legal publishing solutions.

    - Conduct legal research to verify statutory history, citations, references and legal authorities, and develop legislative roadmaps and implementation plans.
    - Actively work with AI-generated legal content by reviewing, validating and refining outputs to ensure legal accuracy, completeness and adherence to editorial standards.
    - Conduct proof review and quality control across print and digital platforms and support updates to court rules and regulatory content.
    - Collaborate with commercial partners, content editors and technology teams on new product development and content expansion initiatives.
    - Address external customer questions and complaints and prepare professional customer-facing responses.

Requirements

  • LLB or equivalent law degree required and attorney admission.
    - Strong legal research, analytical, editing and writing skills.
    - Interest in statutory law, legal publishing and the application of AI and emerging technologies in legal workflows.
    - High attention to detail, commitment to quality and strong organisational skills.
    - Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
    - Strong communication, collaboration and problem-solving skills.
    - Proficiency with Microsoft Office, content management systems and comfort learning new tools, including AI-enabled platforms.
    - Experience in legal publishing, legislative analysis or regulatory content management; experience with XML, structured content and digital publishing systems; and experience with proof review, publication workflows and print and digital production processes.

We promote a healthy work/life balance across the organisation. We offer an appealing working prospect for our people. With numerous wellbeing initiatives, shared parental leave, study assistance and sabbaticals, we will help you meet your immediate responsibilities and your long-term goals.

Working flexible hours - flexing the times when you work in the day to help you fit everything in and work when you are the most productive.

LexisNexis Legal & Professional® provides legal, regulatory, and business information and analytics that help customers increase their productivity, improve decision-making, achieve better outcomes, and advance the rule of law around the world.
